title: He studied why India's own town councils don't work. It won him political science's top prize.
sources: Duke University Trinity College of Arts & Sciences, 2026 - Award-Winning Research Sheds Light on 'Who Knows How to Govern?'
Political Science Now, 2026 - Adam Auerbach, Shikhar Singh, and Tariq Thachil Receive the 2026 Heinz I. Eulau Award
caption:
He wanted to know why India's small-town councils keep underperforming. The answer won him one of political science's most prestigious awards.

Shikhar Singh, Assistant Professor of Political Science at Duke University, received the 2026 Heinz I. Eulau Award alongside co-authors Adam Auerbach and Tariq Thachil, for their American Political Science Review article on India's municipal governance. Their fieldwork in India's small-town councils found elected officials often lack the basic procedural knowledge to actually govern - a factor overlooked in most accountability research. Singh has also written 'Migrants and Machine Politics' (Princeton University Press, 2023), which has won four separate major prizes, including APSA's own Best Book award.

He didn't study governance from a distance - he went into India's own town halls to find out what was actually missing.
